findings.summary: The new entries are not marked prose-only, although the `mechanism` default applies to this job and nothing in the code enforces either rule.
findings.evidence: The `mechanism` default (defaults.toml:71) says rules that matter are enforced by mechanism or explicitly marked prose-only. outcome-check, no-empty-success and thrash-stop all end with 'Prose-only: no loop code ... yet.' Nothing enforces hermetic-checks. checks.rs:534 clears the environment, but the tests (checks.rs:749 and others) pass PATH back in, so tools are still found on PATH, and no code records which tool was used when a fallback replaces the preferred one. Nothing enforces version-pins either, apart from the Claude pin (D154) and `--locked`. The plan's new test proves only that the text exists, not that the rule is followed. Fix: End each entry with a sentence after the first one, for example: 'Prose-only: only the Claude Code pin (D154) and --locked enforce it today.' and 'Prose-only: checks.rs still finds tools on PATH; job 20261025-183644-t67q's follow-up adds the mechanism.' Only the first sentence is rendered, so the reader budget does not change. Optionally have the new test assert that `Prose-only` appears in each full statement.

findings.summary: The version-pins entry says 'one explicit command' but does not name the command that already exists.
findings.evidence: D154 (docs/decisions.md:4213-4233) added `cargo run -p xtask -- repin`. It is implemented at xtask/src/main.rs:50 and 686, documented at README.md:282, and the claude.rs:58 refusal message points to it. So the command does not need to be built. A reader or producer who sees only the generic wording may propose building one. Fix: In the second sentence of version-pins, name `cargo run -p xtask -- repin` (D154) as the command for the Claude Code pin, and say that other pins follow the same exact-pin rule. Cite D154 in D181's Provenance. Do not touch xtask.
findings.location: Plan step 1; reading's Out of scope ('An xtask repin command ... building it is a separate job')

findings.summary: D181 should say openly that it reverses an earlier recorded decision against raising this same budget.
findings.evidence: Decisions at docs/decisions.md:4856, 4897 and 4935 each reject a budget raise because 'budgets never rise to fit a set'. D170 (4935) rejected raising the reader budget specifically. lib.rs:178 states the same rule. The plan rewords the comment so it covers only the producer and verifier budgets, but step 7 does not say D181 names the earlier rule it departs from or why the 'pay with a removal' option fails here. Fix: In D181's Decision or Alternatives, cite the rule and D170 by name. Say that this raise is a deliberate exception because new defaults are policy content that cannot be traded for removing other defaults within this job's scope. Note that the reader budget was raised before: 1800 to 1930 in D93, and again for behavior-evidence (decisions.md:613).

findings.summary: The prose about hermetic checks could easily use a word the boundary scan bans.
findings.evidence: boundary_words() (xtask/tests/policy.rs:88-115) bans words such as the 'sand'+'box' family and the 'oper'+'ator' family, and these come up naturally when writing about isolated or ambient check environments. The plan writes 'person running Athena', which passes, but it gives the producer no warning. Fix: In step 2, tell the producer to avoid the boundary-word families when writing about isolation (say 'hermetic' or 'isolated' instead), and to run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` after editing the prose.
findings.location: Plan steps 2, 7 and 8; Dependents entry on xtask/tests/policy.rs

request_reading_mismatch: None for the plan. One factual error in the reading: its Out-of-scope note says an xtask repin command still has to be built, but it already exists (D154; xtask/src/main.rs:686). This does not change the plan's scope.
summary: I read defaults.rs, defaults.toml, lib.rs:172-185, run_pin_tests.rs:1595-1645, budgets.rs:1-140, briefs.rs, live.rs, checks.rs, xtask/src/main.rs, policy.rs, CHANGELOG.md and decisions.md (D154, D170 and the entries that say "budgets never rise"). The plan's citations hold. render() prints only the first sentence, cut at the first ". " (defaults.rs:58-83). REPO_DEFAULTS is at defaults.rs:89. The reader budget is set at lib.rs:176. The only literal `of 2000` in code is at run_pin_tests.rs:1625. budgets.rs computes the reader set from the real defaults.toml and compares it with system-facts.md:25. live.rs no longer pins the reader figure, and no test counts the real defaults entries or pins their byte size. The dependents list matches what grep finds. I estimate the two new rendered lines at about 140-145 tokens (bytes/3, not measured), so the set lands near 2140, under 2200. The test for criterion 6 fails on the base tree because get() returns None, and it uses the production parse and render with no double. All eight criteria have a working demonstration. I found no blocker or major problem. Four minor issues remain. (1) Neither new entry says "prose-only", although the `mechanism` default applies and three existing entries follow that convention. (2) The version-pins entry does not name the repin command that already exists (D154, `cargo run -p xtask -- repin`). (3) D181 should state openly that it departs from the rule that budgets never rise to fit a set, which D170 used to reject exactly this budget raise. (4) The prose about hermetic checks could easily slip into a word the boundary scan bans.
